subject: Operational reserve proposal and monthly credit allocation for SLA template
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.infer>
To: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@everlane.io>, Everlane Ops <ops@everlane.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.infer>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.infer>
Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational reserve proposal and monthly credit allocation for SLA template

Hi Carlos / Everlane team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I've pulled together a short proposal for how Redwood would treat an "operational reserve" in the SLA and how monthly service credits would be allocated across your hosted and batch inference workloads. The goal is to preserve a clear uptime baseline for low-latency (interactive) endpoints while acknowledging predictable maintenance and capacity reservation behavior for batched jobs.

Key points up front:
- Baseline uptime: 99.90% for interactive endpoints (standard).
- Batched / scheduled inference: proposal to set a separate operational baseline at 99.70% with explicit maintenance carveouts to cover nightly windows.
- Monthly credit model: hybrid approach — a capped monthly credit pool (proportional to committed spend) + per-incident credit for outages that exceed the reserve.

Attachment: redwood-sla-opreserve-proposal.pdf contains the math and two worked examples based on your traffic profile (attached sample-credit-calcs.xlsx used to generate the scenarios).

Questions we have for you:
1) Any regulatory or internal procurement constraints that require a single uptime metric across all product surfaces?
2) Do you anticipate >3 maintenance windows/month for batch pipelines during peak season (Nov–Jan)?
3) Preferred granularity for alerting/tracing to support per-incident credit adjudication (request IDs vs. route-level)?

Requested next steps:
- Carlos: confirm whether Everlane legal is open to a dual-baseline construct for batch vs interactive.
- Ben / Laura: if Everlane confirms we can scope this, Ben will produce a redline that plugs the operational reserve language into the standard SLA template.

Thanks — happy to walk through the attachment with your procurement/legal team on Monday.

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.infer
+1 (415) 555-0182

Redwood Inference — production-first inference runtime
From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@everlane.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.infer>
Cc: Everlane Legal <legal@everlane.io>, Everlane Ops <ops@everlane.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.infer>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational reserve proposal and monthly credit allocation for SLA template

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the clear summary and the materials. We reviewed the PDF with our ops and finance leads. A few quick notes: 

- We like the hybrid monthly-pool + per-incident approach in principle. Gives us predictability while preserving incentive alignment.
- Our legal preference is usually to have a single table of uptime thresholds in the contract. Splitting baseline by workload type is acceptable only if it is very explicit and there is a mapping table (i.e., route prefixes -> baseline).
- From ops: we do expect more maintenance in Nov–Jan (holiday deployments and data re-ingest). Plan for up to 6 scheduled maintenance windows in peak months.

Two asks from our side before we can sign off on the dual-baseline: 
1) Can you provide a simple mapping example showing route prefixes for interactive vs. batch and how credits would flow if an incident crosses both surfaces?
2) Please confirm the maximum monthly credit cap as a % of committed spend and propose how credits are prorated if multiple incidents occur in a single month.

Cc'ing legal to start the contract thread.

—Carlos
Head of Platform Engineering, Everlane
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.infer>
To: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@everlane.io>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.infer>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.infer>, Everlane Legal <legal@everlane.io>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational reserve proposal and monthly credit allocation for SLA template

Carlos — appreciated. I pulled together the requested examples and a proposed credit cap ladder. High level:

- Route mapping: interactive -> /v1/generate, /v1/chat; batch -> /v1/batch/*, /v1/ingest/*; we will add a supplemental appendix that lists exact prefixes and examples so legal can see the operational mapping.
- Monthly credit cap proposal: tiered by committed spend (example):
  - < $50k/mo -> cap = 2% of monthly spend
  - $50k–$250k/mo -> cap = 4%
  - > $250k/mo -> cap = 6%
- Multiple incidents in a month: credits are additive up to the cap; per-incident credits are computed as % of monthly spend proportional to minutes of outage weighted by affected traffic percentage (worked example in the spreadsheet).

On the cross-surface incident question: if an outage impacts both interactive and batch routes concurrently, we propose crediting against the higher-impact surface only (i.e., if interactive latency is degraded, use interactive bucket) to avoid double-crediting. We'll document that in the appendix and include wording to let either party request an audit if they think allocation was incorrect.

I've attached the worked examples (sample-credit-calcs.xlsx) and will follow up with an appendix doc for route mapping.

Action: Laura — can you review the proposed caps and the audit clause language before we send a redline?

Ben
Director, Sales Engineering
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.infer>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.infer>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.infer>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@everlane.io>, Everlane Legal <legal@everlane.io>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational reserve proposal and monthly credit allocation for SLA template

Thanks team — quick read-through and a few contract-focused edits:

1) Cap mechanics: I recommend using a floor cap for small customers (1% min) to avoid zero-credit months for low-spend pilots; Ben's ladder looks good but add a 1% floor.
2) Maintenance carveouts: define "scheduled maintenance" as events with >=72h notice for anything over 2 hours, and maintain a monthly visibility report for windows shorter than 2 hours.
3) Cross-surface incidents: instead of "higher-impact surface only", propose the following language — primary surface defined by percentage of affected RPS for the incident window; if within 10% between surfaces, the incident is considered "cross-surface" and an independent adjudication path (audit + 3rd party logs) applies.

If Everlane is comfortable with that, we will prepare a redline tomorrow that plugs the operational reserve language into section 3.1 of the SLA and includes the appendix for route mapping and credit maths.

I will also add a DocuSign stub to accelerate execution once redlines are agreed.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@everlane.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.infer>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.infer>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.infer>
Cc: Everlane Legal <legal@everlane.io>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational reserve proposal and monthly credit allocation for SLA template

Laura — thanks, that language addresses our internal concerns. The 72h threshold for long maintenance is sensible and the floor cap solves procurement edge cases. Please send the redline and the appendix; our legal team will aim to review within 48 hours.

Two small asks before sign:
- Can Redwood include an example clause for expedited mitigation collaboration (a 4-hour war-room cadence for Sev-1 incidents) and a named point of contact for 24/7 escalation?
- Confirm DocuSign link when the redline is uploaded.

If those items are included, we should be able to finalize and route for signatures next week.

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to the redline.

—Carlos
Head of Platform Engineering, Everlane
